source.title: How to Choose Cables and Switchgear for Solar and Wind Projects in India
source.body:
A solar farm or wind plant is only as dependable as the electrical network behind it. Panels and turbines generate the power, but cables, terminations and switchgear carry, protect and control it for 20–25 years. Bharat Trading Corporation (BTC), a Pune-based supplier of wires, cables and switchgear, explains how to choose these components. For the full walkthrough, read our[ Cable and Switchgear Selection Guide for Renewable Energy (Solar/Wind) Installations](https://btc.net.in/cable-and-switchgear-selection-guide-for-renewable-energy-solar-wind-installations/).
Why Component Selection Matters
Renewable sites face sun, heat, rain, dust and vibration every day. Weak insulation or poorly matched switchgear leads to voltage loss, insulation failure and unplanned shutdowns. Specifying correctly at the start means fewer maintenance visits and a better-protected investment. BTC’s[ renewable energy industry page](https://btc.net.in/renewable-energy-industry/) shows how this applies across solar, wind, hydro and hybrid plants.
Follow the Power: Where Each Component Fits
DC collection: Solar DC cables connect panels to combiner boxes and inverters.
Conversion: Inverters or turbine controllers convert DC to AC.
AC distribution: Armoured or heavy-duty power cables feed switchgear, breakers, control panels and transformers.
Monitoring: Control and instrumentation cables support SCADA and automation.
Export or storage: Well-terminated wiring carries energy to the grid or battery systems.
Choosing the Right Cables
Solar DC cables (single and twin core): Built for high DC voltage, UV exposure and outdoor weather. See BTC’s[ solar cable](https://btc.net.in/product/solar-cable-is-17293/).
Armoured and unarmoured power cables: Used for AC distribution and transformer connections. Armoured types add protection for underground or exposed runs.
Control and instrumentation cables: Keep monitoring and plant automation accurate.
Copper vs aluminium: Copper gives higher conductivity and compact sizing. Aluminium is lighter and more economical for long runs across large solar farms.
FRLS vs LSZH: FRLS limits flame spread and smoke. LSZH releases minimal smoke and no halogen gases, which suits enclosed plant rooms.
Explore the full range of[ wires and cables](https://btc.net.in/product-category/wires-and-cables/), including[ RR Kabel](https://btc.net.in/rr-kable-supplier/) and[ Dynamic Cable](https://btc.net.in/dynamic-cable-supplier/).
Terminations and Protective Accessories
A cable is only as reliable as its connection. BTC supplies[ cable lugs and glands](https://btc.net.in/product-category/lugs-gland/) for secure, vibration-resistant terminations, heat shrink sleeves for weatherproof sealing, and[ cable ducts](https://btc.net.in/product-category/cable-ducts/) and[ cable ties](https://btc.net.in/product-category/cable-tie/) for organised, maintainable wiring.
Switchgear for Renewable Installations
Once AC power leaves the inverter or turbine controller, switchgear controls, protects and isolates circuits. This lets operators de-energise one section for maintenance without shutting down the whole plant. BTC supplies[ switchgear](https://btc.net.in/product-category/switchgear/) through Schneider Electric, so you can[ view our Schneider Electric supplier page](https://btc.net.in/schneider-electric-supplier/). Match it to site conditions such as outdoor exposure, temperature swings, dust and moisture. Sourcing cables and switchgear together helps teams plan distribution, protection and control as one coordinated system.
Challenges to Plan For
Plan for UV and weather exposure, 600V–1500V DC stress in solar systems, turbine vibration, moisture in hydro plants, corrosion near coastal sites, and voltage drop over long runs.
